ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's own sanctions list (Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Additionally, all beneficial owners, directors, and senior managers must be screened against the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) public statements and the Korean FIU's list of high-risk jurisdictions. PEPs (Politically Exposed Persons) must undergo enhanced due diligence, including source of funds verification and senior management approval. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least quarterly), and upon any trigger event. All results must be documented and retained for at least 5 years. The screening process must be automated with manual override capabilities, and any hits must be escalated to the compliance officer for resolution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea, Company Registration Information System (CRIS) - 인터넷등기소
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean script (Hangul). For foreign entities, a phonetic transliteration into Hangul is required. The name must consist of a distinctive element, a business purpose descriptor, and a legal form suffix (e.g., '유한회사' for LLC). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. Four-tier naming conventions: (1) distinctive name, (2) business type, (3) legal form, (4) optional additional descriptors.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Book III Companies, Chapter V Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 543 through 568; together with the Employment Security Act, Articles 18, 20 and 23 for the statutory paid private employment placement business license applicable to executive search and headhunting services.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: District Court Registration Office having territorial jurisdiction over the registered principal office of the company; for a Seoul-headquartered company, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Registration Application for a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), submitted together with notarized Articles of Incorporation and supporting capital payment records.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean law imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The members may fix the capital amount in the Articles of Incorporation, but all declared contributions must be paid in full before the incorporation registration is filed. No blocked or escrow account is required beyond the bank-issued capital deposit certificate; the deposited subscription funds are released after the registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA, A LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. RESOLUTION NO. 1, adopted this [●] day of [●], 2025, at [●] Korean Standard Time, at the Company's registered office at [●], Republic of Korea. A meeting of the Board of Directors of the Company was duly convened and held with all directors present or, in the case of a sole director, the sole director acted by written resolution in lieu of a meeting. [●] chaired the meeting and confirmed that the meeting was properly noticed, that a quorum existed, and that the resolutions below were considered in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and the Commercial Act. After due deliberation, the Board unanimously resolved as follows. 1. Capital Subscription and Payment. The Board reviewed the Articles of Incorporation, the member register, and the certified bank deposit statement. The Board confirmed that the full amount of member contributions constituting the stated capital of KRW [●] has been lawfully subscribed by the members and paid in full into the designated bank account before the commencement of incorporation registration. The Board ratified the capital contribution schedule and authorized the release of deposited funds after completion of the statutory incorporation registration. 2. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company shall be [●], as stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The registered office is the domestic legal seat of the Company, and all statutory summonses, governmental notices, court communications, and corporate filings shall be served at this address. The Representative Director was directed to notify the competent registration court and all administrative agencies of any future change of address. 3. Bank Mandate. The Company shall open a corporate bank account with [●] Bank, [●] Branch, for the deposit and management of paid-in capital, and shall maintain an operating account after issuance of the business registration certificate for client retainers, placement fees, and payments. [●], [●], and [●] are appointed as authorized signatories. Any two authorized signatories shall sign all checks, wire instructions, and payment orders, including domestic wire and cross-border payment instructions processed through Wise B2B. No borrowing, guarantee, pledge, or issuance of guarantees shall be executed by any officer without prior board approval. 4. Statutory Officers. The following individuals are appointed to hold office: [●] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [●] as Director and Chief Operating Officer; [●] as Director and Corporate Secretary; and [●] as Auditor. Each appointee accepts office in writing. The Representative Director is vested with the fullest authority permitted by law to represent the Company in all dealings with courts, tax authorities, banks, clients, and the Ministry of Employment and Labor, and to execute all documents, sign service contracts, open bank accounts, and oversee corporate governance compliance. 5. Regulatory Authorization. The Representative Director is specifically authorized to file the incorporation registration, business registration with the National Tax Service, mandatory social insurance registrations, and the private employment placement business registration/permit under the Employment Security Act for executive search and headhunting operations, and to engage licensed attorneys, certified labor attorneys, and administrative agents as necessary. 6. Effectiveness. This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force until amended by a later resolution of the Board or the general meeting of members.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization, and Capital Deposit for Yuhan Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public and a licensed commercial bank located in the district of the intended registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must prepare the Articles of Incorporation for the Yuhan Hoesa, setting out the corporate name, objects limited to executive search, headhunting, human resources consulting, and employment placement, the head office address, total capital, the value and type of each member's contribution, and the number and tenures of directors and auditor. Every member must sign and affix a seal or signature on the Articles, after which the document is notarized by a Korean notary public. A temporary corporate account is then opened in the name of the intended company; each member transfers the full amount of his or her contribution from his or her own account, and the bank issues a capital deposit certificate. No statutory minimum capital applies, but the declared contributions must be paid in full before the incorporation registration is filed. If any contribution is made in kind, the asset transfer and title registration must be completed before filing. All bank receipts and notarized copies must be retained because the registration court will verify the capital deposit certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation signed by all members
Valid national ID or passport copies of all members
Power of attorney if an agent will execute the acts
Bank-issued capital deposit certificate for the full subscription amount
Notarial certificate of the Articles of Incorporation
Draft object clause covering ISIC 7830 executive search and headhunting services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or bank questions the corporate name, object clause, or identity of members, the Articles of Incorporation must be amended and re-executed with full member consent. The capital deposit can remain in the temporary account during correction, and a revised notarized version must be submitted before proceeding to court registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registration Office with jurisdiction over the registered principal office, e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the notarized Articles and capital deposit certificate, the applicant must file the Incorporation Registration Application for a Limited Liability Company with the competent court registration office. The filing may be made physically or, where available, through the Supreme Court online registration system. The registration office will verify the availability and lawfulness of the corporate name, the object clause, the identity and contributions of members, the validity and notarization of the Articles, the appointment of directors and auditor, and the full payment of capital. The applicant must also submit the registered seal report and pay the registration tax and court fees. If the registry clerk issues a supplemental or correction order, the applicant must cure the deficiencies within the statutory correction period, ordinarily ten calendar days, by filing corrected instruments, identification documents, or additional consents through the same registry. Once accepted, the registry issues the Certificate of Company Registration, which legally establishes the Yuhan Hoesa and enables all subsequent operational filings.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Registration Application for a Limited Liability Company
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank capital deposit certificate
List of members and the amount and method of each contribution
Written appointment and acceptance letters of directors and auditor
Registered company seal report
Payment receipt for registration tax and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, the applicant must submit the requested supplements within the statutory cure period. If the application is rejected or deemed withdrawn, the applicant should promptly correct the defective item, pay the applicable fee again if required, and resubmit a clean application with the same or revised Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Business Registration and Mandatory Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through Hometax or the local district tax office, together with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and local Employment and Labor Office for social insurance enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registry issues the Certificate of Company Registration, the Representative Director must apply for a Business Registration Certificate with the National Tax Service no later than twenty days after the business begins. The application must be filed through the Hometax electronic portal using the corporate certificate, or in person at the district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered office. The application package must include the Certificate of Company Registration, certified copies of the Articles of Incorporation, the office lease contract with the landlord's written consent to use the premises as a business office, the Representative Director's identification, and the intended business opening date. Once the Business Registration Certificate is issued, the company must enroll in the four mandatory social insurance schemes: national pension, national health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance. The company must also open its operating bank account, register the company seal with the bank, and complete value-added tax taxpayer registration for the expected executive search and headhunting turnover.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Company Registration from the court registry
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Business Registration Application form
Office lease contract with landlord's use consent
Representative Director's identification and corporate authentication certificate
Bank account details and anticipated business opening date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Hometax rejects or queries the application, the Representative Director should respond through the portal with the missing documentation. If the landlord consent is defective, a new signed consent and certified copy of the lease must be obtained and submitted. If the business registration is delayed, the company may still proceed with licensing only after the tax certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Paid Private Employment Placement Business Registration/Permit for Executive Search and Headhunting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Employment and Labor, specifically the local regional employment and labor office having jurisdiction over the company's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the company's scope is paid executive search and headhunting, it must obtain a Paid Private Employment Placement Business Registration/Permit under the Employment Security Act before accepting client retainers or charging placement fees. The Representative Director must submit the prescribed application to the local employment and labor office together with the Business Registration Certificate, certified Articles of Incorporation, proof of office ownership or lease, an office floor plan and facility description, staffing details, the proposed fee schedule, placement contract templates, and candidate protection rules. The labor office will review the applicant's record, office suitability, financial capacity, and ability to comply with statutory restrictions on charging job seekers. After approval, the permit must be displayed at the registered office, and any change of address, CEO, trade name, or business scope must be reported to the labor office. Placement contracts, invoices, and recruitment records must be retained for at least three years.
required_dossiers: Paid Private Employment Placement Business Registration/Permit application form
Business Registration Certificate
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Office lease or ownership certificate with floor area evidence
Proposed fee schedule and placement contract templates
Candidate protection policy and employment placement service rules
Identification and qualification record of the responsible manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the employment and labor office requests correction or returns the application, the company must cure the stated deficiency, such as an incomplete fee schedule, insufficient office evidence, or missing responsible manager qualifications, and resubmit immediately. If the permit is denied, the company may file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Employment and Labor or seek judicial review, but must not operate paid placement services until the permit is validly issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Employment and Labor, Employment Policy Bureau and local regional employment and labor office; for physical industrial and environmental permits, Not Applicable because this is an office-based executive search and headhunting activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Paid Private Employment Placement Business Registration/Permit under the Employment Security Act of the Republic of Korea, covering executive search, C-suite headhunting, and specialist technology recruitment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment engagement is not required for the office-based ISIC 7830 operations; if a separate physical tenant improvement project occurs, the local building authority would be the relevant body, not the environmental assessment agency.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no Full Environmental Impact Assessment, Environmental Registration, or Prelimited Environmental Review is required because the activity is not listed in the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act and does not involve manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, warehousing, or physical industrial facilities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None applicable - there are no industrial wastewater, air pollutant, VOC, odor, or hazardous waste generation thresholds for executive search headhunting offices. The company is only subject to ordinary municipal wastewater and solid waste disposal rules, and if it later adds warehouses, assembly, or light manufacturing, a new EIA screening and industrial licensing analysis will be required before that operation commences.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for Civil Defense industrial fire permits. The office must obtain a fire-fighting system completion inspection certificate and general fire safety inspection under the Fire Services Act before occupancy, and the employer must file a safety and health start-up report under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for the workplace. Structural load approval is not required unless the company alters the building; if tenant improvements are made, a building alteration permit or report to the local government will be necessary.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through district tax offices and the online HomeTax Service at hometax.go.kr; the competent district tax office is the tax office that has jurisdiction over the registered Korean head office of the Yuhan Hoesa. Customs export clearance is administered separately by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Korean Yuhan Hoesa: (1) complete commercial registration with the Korean Commercial Registration Court; (2) within 20 days of business commencement, file the business registration application with the NTS district tax office using HomeTax or direct filing; (3) submit the articles of incorporation, certificate of commercial registration, foreign shareholder identification or passport and applicable notarized translations, proof of the Korean place of business such as a lease or title document, and the corporate resolution appointing the representative; (4) the NTS will then issue the Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which is the statutory taxpayer identification number used for corporate income tax, VAT, payroll withholding, and electronic tax invoices; (5) for a foreign non-resident entity that has no domestic Korean establishment but makes taxable supplies in Korea, the foreign entity must separately register as a foreign VAT business operator with the NTS through HomeTax or the competent tax office and, where required by the NTS, appoint a Korean tax representative to receive the tax ID certificate, file VAT returns, and receive official communications; (6) the BRN must be quoted on all tax invoices issued and on all customs declarations where goods are cleared.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a separate legal person and is mandatorily classified as a Korean domestic corporation subject to entity-level Korean corporate income tax on its worldwide income. Korea has no check-the-box election, no pass-through LLC election, and no domestic hybrid-entity election. A foreign jurisdiction may classify the Yuhan Hoesa differently for foreign tax purposes, but the NTS will disregard any such foreign classification for Korean tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 - there is no statutory economic turnover threshold. A Korean corporate entity that begins business activities is required to register as a VAT business operator from business commencement regardless of expected revenue. The simplified taxable person scheme is limited to eligible individual proprietors below the statutory turnover ceiling and does not exempt a corporate Yuhan Hoesa from VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Corporate VAT payers are mandatory electronic tax invoice users. The electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) must be issued through the NTS HomeTax system or through an NTS-approved e-invoice service provider integrated with HomeTax APIs. The e-tax invoice data must be transmitted to the NTS by the day after the invoice is issued. Korea does not operate a Latin-American-style real-time pre-issuance fiscal clearance or digital stamping system; anti-fraud integrity is enforced through digital-certificate authentication, mandatory issuance for B2B supplies, automatic cross-matching of purchase-side and sales-side VAT records, and NTS audit powers. For a B2B executive-search and headhunting agency, e-invoicing is the required fiscal path for all domestic supplies, and zero-rated export supplies must also be reported through the VAT return with the export evidence retained.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, exports of goods and qualifying foreign-currency-earning services are zero-rated. For the Yuhan Hoesa executive-search and headhunting business, zero-rating is available when the service is supplied to a non-resident client and the service is not consumed for the benefit of a Korean domestic business. The zero-rated export treatment must be evidenced by a contract with the overseas client, a fee charged in foreign currency, actual receipt of the fees from outside Korea within the statutory foreign-exchange collection period, and an electronic tax invoice issued under the zero-rated code. If the foreign-invoiced service in fact benefits a Korean operating company or a Korean resident employer, the NTS will recharacterize the supply as domestic and assess 10% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Certificate) issued via the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system - applicable only to goods exports, not to pure service export
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill - applicable only to physical goods movement, not applicable to executive-search services
Executed executive-search or headhunting services agreement with the non-resident client, identifying the parties, scope, fee, and place of benefit or use of services
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice transmitted through HomeTax, marked as export/zero-rated under the Korean VAT Act
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of the foreign currency consideration
Bank statement or SWIFT credit record showing the foreign currency receipt and demonstrating compliance with the statutory 180-day repatriation/collection deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If export zero-rating is claimed without the required export documentation, foreign-exchange receipt evidence, or customer documentation, the NTS may retrospectively disallow the zero rate, reassess the full 10% VAT on the invoiced amount, and impose statutory additional taxes for underpayment, late payment, and negligent or fraudulent returns. Fraudulent or intentionally unsubstantiated export zero-rating claims can trigger the criminal tax-evasion penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes, including imprisonment and fines up to three times the evaded tax, together with extensions of the statute of limitation up to 10 years for false or fraudulent returns. The taxpayer bears the burden of producing and retaining all export service contracts, electronic tax invoices, foreign exchange receipts, and placement evidence for at least the full statutory retention period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the primary foreign-exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA); the Bank of Korea acts as the central monetary supervisory authority and oversees the reporting and clearing infrastructure for the won and foreign-currency accounts held through domestic foreign-exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised, largely market-based current account convertibility regime. The won is not freely convertible outside the country; official settlement and client FX conversion must occur through Korean financial institutions. Capital account transactions are generally permitted but require report to the Ministry of Economy and Finance on a post-transaction basis or prior report for foreign direct investment and offshore loans under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account payments, including service fees, royalties and executive-search retainer fees, are freely convertible through foreign exchange banks subject to transaction evidence. There are no pooled surrender obligations; the export proceeds receipt rules impose a collection deadline and route through a domestic foreign-exchange bank, although there is no mandatory conversion ratio. Profit remittance barriers are minimal for a properly documented dividend distribution; withholding tax rates apply according to the relevant tax treaty. For a headhunting export-of-services model, retainers invoiced abroad received in USD may be held in foreign-currency deposit accounts, or converted to KRW for payroll, without prior approval, provided the corresponding underlying contract and invoice documentation are retained.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from both goods and services must be collected through a domestic foreign-exchange bank. Under the Foreign Exchange Transaction Regulations, a services exporter such as an executive-search firm must normally obtain collection of foreign currency proceeds within 180 days from the invoice date or completion of services; extensions up to two years are available at the discretion of the designated foreign-exchange bank in cases of force majeure, litigation or demonstrable collection delays. There is no mandatory conversion ratio in the sense of a surrender requirement to the Bank of Korea; the statutory ratio is effectively 0% of export proceeds required to be converted to won. Exporters may retain the foreign currency in a designated foreign-currency deposit account or convert to KRW based on operational treasury needs. Evidence such as the underlying export contract, service completion report, invoice, and receivable ledger must be maintained and presented to the handling bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / USD Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally restricted. Wise B2B and other offshore digital EMIs are not licensed as foreign-exchange banks under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and cannot act as the primary settlement rail for export service proceeds. Under the statutory framework, all export proceeds from a Korean LLC must be received through a Korean foreign-exchange bank, and corporate operating accounts for a resident Korean entity must be settled at a licensed domestic bank. A foreign EMI can only function as a non-bank payment initiation interface for low-risk discretionary disbursements, while the actual clearing and settlement still runs through a Korean-licensed bank. Relying on a foreign EMI as the exclusive cross-border treasury rail would create an FX booking gap, violate the export-proceeds receipt discipline, and likely lead to a bank compliance rejection at the account-opening stage.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch appearance is generally mandatory for a foreign statutory director opening a Korean corporate operating account. Most Tier-1 Korean banks require the statutory director or a delegated Korean finance officer with a properly notarised and apostilled corporate power of attorney to appear physically at the branch for identity verification, face-to-face AML interview, and account signing. Remote consular proxy opening without any physical presence is not accepted for an active treasury or operational account, although certain banks allow a video KYC follow-up after the in-branch session. For a foreign-owned Korean LLC used for executive search, the prudent route is to have the local Korean resident director appear with the corporate secretarial file; if no local director exists, a foreign director must either travel to Korea or grant a specific corporate power of attorney to a designated Korean resident officer with the original power of attorney verified at a Korean consulate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a foreign parent holding company in a complex equity chain, with nominee directors and unclear control over the Korean LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete natural-person Beneficial Ownership register with tax IDs, passports, and personal residential addresses; apostilled corporate registry extract, articles of incorporation, share register, and a corporate tree chart covering all intermediate entities; bank reference letters from the home institution of each significant shareholder; signed declarations confirming no sanctions, PEP, or unexplained fund source; notarised Korean director identity documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The executive-search entity requires a statutory licence under the Occupational Security Act, but the bank cannot verify the licence during onboarding, creating an unlicensed-business risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Employment Agency Permit issued by the competent local government authority for fee-charging job placement; a copy of the Ministry of Employment and Labor inspection or registration acknowledgement; service contracts demonstrating permissible headhunting activity; the firm's internal compliance manual and AML policy; designation of the Chief Financial Officer as the corporate account compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Retainer collections arrive from a small number of offshore clients in high-risk or tax-haven jurisdictions, and some remittances are channelled through third-party payment platforms such as Wise B2B, creating trade-based money-laundering indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-client KYC pack including signed executive-search retainer agreement, itemised invoice, the paying client's own bank statement or verified payment history, the client's corporate registration, and the ultimate beneficiary sign-off on the placement; a senior management attestation explaining the commercial reason for using an intermediary; sanctions screening results against UN, EU, OFAC and Korean FIU lists; negative-media and adverse-news screening on each foreign payor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The operating account shows mixed use of a KRW operational account, a USD foreign-currency deposit account, and rapid round-tripping of converted funds for domestic payroll, which may resemble layering or receivables financing from an undisclosed lender.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A twelve-month cash-flow forecast and Treasury policy document; payroll ledger with corresponding tax filings; vendor invoices and evidence of performance for each notable disbursement; a reconciliation of the USD deposit account with each retainer receipt and the corresponding invoice number; monthly VAT and withholding tax returns; a bank-comfort letter from any lender; and a signed treasury declaration that all FX conversions are backed by genuine service exports and supplier liabilities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All foreign capital injections into the Korean LLC must be routed through a designated foreign-exchange bank. Before remittance, the foreign investor must complete a Foreign Investor Registration with the handling bank or Kotra. The remittance itself must be a SWIFT MT103 marked with the correct Bank of Korea transaction purpose code for foreign direct investment, identified as share subscription or capital increase. Upon receipt, the bank issues a foreign-investment deposit confirmation and the investor must file a Foreign Investment Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, normally within 30 days. For capital verification, the bank provides a Capital Deposit Certificate for the corporate registry; the LLC then completes the paid-in-capital registration with the Seoul District Court. If the funds will be converted to KRW, the conversion must be executed through the same handling bank on a spot basis with proper trade-evidence retention. Parent-company loans above the regulatory threshold must be reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the handling bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act using the relevant external borrowing purpose code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For external service payments such as subcontractor placement fees, software subscriptions, marketing purchases or repayment of shareholder loans, the LLC instructs its bank to execute SWIFT MT103 transfers with the full invoice number, contract reference, and tax certificate attached. Comfort letters or documentary evidence for each beneficiary relationship must be pre-filed with the bank. Traditional Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections are not typical for executive-search headhunting, but they remain available to the LLC if it engages in international procurement of technology assets, office equipment purchases, or trade-related transactions with Korean or offshore vendors. Domestic payroll, social security, pension and tax payments are cleared through the local Korean banking and Hometax systems, not through SWIFT. The LLC should maintain monthly reconciliation between cross-border wires and the corresponding export/service invoices to avoid a pattern of broken payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward foreign-exchange contracts against real current-account exposure, specifically USD/KRW forwards with maturity aligned to the invoicing and settlement cycle of the headhunting retainers, supported by the underlying service contracts and receivables schedule.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) entered into with a licensed Korean bank for hedging the KRW/USD exposure of a non-resident parent or foreign institutional borrower, only when the underlying transaction is a Korean foreign-investment asset valuation hedge to protect the capital account, and only through the handling bank as an acceptable substitute for a deliverable forward when offshore settlement is contractually required.

Cross-currency swaps and buy/sell currency swaps permitted strictly for asset-liability management on foreign-currency loans or capital account items, for example swapping USD principal borrowed from a foreign parent into KRW for the LLC's operating needs, provided the swap is booked with a licensed Korean bank and the maturity does not exceed the underlying debt maturity.

Forwards and options are not permitted for speculative uncovered positions; all hedging must be documented with a clear treasury and risk-policy memorandum signed by the statutory director and filed with the bank's FX department.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end (December 31) corporate tax return must be filed by March 31 of the following year; for fiscal years ending other than December 31, within 3 months from the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or underpayment triggers a 20% penalty on unpaid tax (20/100 of unpaid amount), plus 0.025% daily interest on unpaid tax for each day of delinquency; repeated non-filing may lead to tax assessment and potential criminal referral; administrative strike-off is not directly applied but business registration can be forcibly closed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Enterprise Annual Report (for entities with foreign ownership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the end of each fiscal year (for foreign-invested companies that have made a foreign investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,700) and potential restriction on foreign investment incentives; not a strike-off trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Si/Gun/Gu) where the head office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: In principle, filed together with the corporate income tax return by the due date of the corporate tax return (March 31 for December fiscal year-end); some municipalities allow submission by April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: 0.3% of unpaid tax per day up to 75 days; additional 20% negligent tax penalty on underreported amounts; continuous non-compliance may lead to compulsory collection and business closure, but not automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Office / Commercial Registration Renewal (Regular Registration Matters)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Court of Registry (Beopwonsa) / Registration Bureau of the local district court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: There is no annual renewal obligation for the commercial registration itself; however, any change in registered information (directors, registered office, capital) must be filed within 2 weeks of the occurrence; an annual amendment occurs only if there are changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register a change within the statutory window results in administrative fine up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,700); continued failure may result in court-ordered compulsory dissolution upon shareholders' request or ex officio striking-off by the court registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Wage and Salary Payment Report (for employers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual withholding tax payment statement (Jijeong Seoseo) must be submitted by February 10 of the following year for the preceding calendar year; if filed via electronic filing, the deadline is February 15.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission penalty: 20% of the unremitted withholding tax amount; additional interest of 0.025% per day; failure to pay withheld taxes can lead to criminal prosecution for embezzlement of national taxes and possible forced closure of business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Beneficial Ownership Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Financial Services Commission for reporting entities; for non-regulated entities, beneficial ownership changes are reported to the registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For companies subject to the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information, where the company is a reporting entity (not typical for executive search), but as a general corporation, changes in controlling shareholders / ultimate beneficial owners must be recorded in the registry and reported within 4 weeks of any transfer of shares; there is no standalone annual UBO confirmation for non-regulated Yuhan Hoesa.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine for non-disclosure of material ownership facts under the Act on Corporate Governance of Financial Companies (if applicable) or general commercial law; for ordinary corporations, failure to maintain the register of members may result in a negligent fine up to KRW 5,000,000; no direct strike-off but court action possible.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory external audit (by an independent certified public accountant under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies) is mandatory for any Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) if, at the end of the fiscal year, it satisfies any of the following thresholds: (a) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.2 million); (b) total revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.7 million); (c) total employees (average number of regular workers) exceed 100; or (d) if it is a 'deemed public company' under the Capital Market Consolidation Act even if below those thresholds. Additionally, if the company is a subsidiary of a listed parent or is required to prepare consolidated financial statements, an audit may be required irrespective of the company’s individual thresholds. For smaller Yuhan Hoesa entities, an annual external audit may still be required if creditors (e.g. financial institutions) or the shareholders representing at least 10% of issued capital demand it, or if the company elects to have an audit voluntarily.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS, as adopted by the Republic of Korea) for entities meeting the full audit threshold (total assets including subsidiaries exceeding KRW 120 billion or listed/deemed public). For other entities, Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) or the Korea Accounting Standards for Non-Public Entities (KAS-NPE / SME GAAP) apply. If the entity is preparing consolidated financial statements, K-IFRS is mandatory.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Korean Commercial Act and the Act on Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism, every Yuhan Hoesa must maintain an accurate register of members containing the names, addresses, and number of shares of each member. There is no separate annual confirmation requirement for ordinary LLCs, but any transfer of registered shares or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the company and recorded in the register immediately. The company must update the register of members within 2 weeks when a transfer occurs. The ultimate beneficial owner(s) (those holding 10% or more of shares or exercising substantial control) must be disclosed in the company's internal register and, if the company is a 'reporting entity' under the Specific Financial Information Act (which an executive search and headhunting agency is generally not), an annual UBO report must be filed with KoFIU by the end of March. For standard Yuhan Hoesa, the '30-day reporting window' is not applicable; instead, any acquisition of 10% or more of shares or controlling interest must be registered with the registry and the company must reflect the change on its internal register within 2 weeks of the transfer date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Register of Equity Holders)
Register of Directors and Statutory Auditors (if any)
Register of Charges and Pledges on Company Assets
Minute Book (Shareholders' Resolutions and Board Resolutions)
Share Transfer Ledger (Including Beneficial Ownership Details)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – USD 1,600 per year (for a commercial registered office address service and local corporate secretarial agent in Seoul or Busan)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 35,000 per year (for a mandatory statutory audit under K-IFRS or K-GAAP performed by an independent registered CPA firm, depending on revenue size and number of subsidiaries)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9%-24% national progressive (KRW 0-200m: 9%; KRW 200m-20bn: 19%; KRW 20bn-300bn: 21%; over KRW 300bn: 24%) plus 10% local surtax on the national corporate tax, yielding 9.9%-26.4% combined
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME and venture-firm reductions, R&D and human-resource development tax credits (generally 25-50% of eligible expenses), Free Economic Zone / foreign-invested high-tech holiday (100% exemption for first 5 years and 50% for next 2 years), 50% deduction for qualifying technology-transfer income, and job-creation credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; executive-search headhunting fees remain ordinary taxable income with no patent box unless embedded software qualifies separately

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax and Tax-Base Computation Return (CIT Form 21013 / equivalent) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly interim preliminary corporate tax payments)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within 3 months after fiscal year-end; a December 31 year-end company must file by March 31; a one-month extension may be granted on approval, and consolidated tax groups file within 4 months

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1a / Box A-1 - Entity Identification and Non-Resident Shareholder Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business registration number, fiscal year, representative director, country of incorporation, foreign shareholder ownership table, and ultimate beneficial ownership schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare every non-resident shareholder's tax jurisdiction, Tax Residency Certificate, and ownership percentage; a Yuhan Hoesa LLC must disclose all foreign members in the ownership schedule. Attach the international related-party transaction schedule and beneficial ownership declaration; omission exposes the company to withholding on distributions and anti-abuse recharacterization

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2d / Box A-2 - Taxable Income Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income under IFRS or K-GAAP, plus add-backs for non-deductible expenses such as unsubstantiated management fees, entertainment in excess, fines, and donations above statutory ceilings, minus tax-exempt income, loss carryforward, and special deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border executive-search fees are deductible only when actual services, arm's-length compensation evidence, and foreign recipient documentation are maintained. Parent-company overhead allocations must be substantiated under Korean transfer-pricing rules and added back if not supported; this line must reconcile to audited financial statements

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 / Box B-2 - Computed Corporate Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive CIT schedule to taxable income, add separate tax on capital gains if any, and calculate national corporate tax before credits and reductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC is entity-level taxed and non-resident shareholders do not compute its liability. If the NTS finds a place of management or permanent establishment in Korea, worldwide income becomes taxable; the 10% local surtax is imposed on the national corporate tax. Foreign-sourced retainer income must be excluded only if no PE exists and income is not attributable to Korea

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 / Box B-3 - Credits, Reductions and Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Subtract SME/Venture tax reductions, R&D credits, job-creation credits, foreign tax credits, and applicable minimum tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits claimed on outbound source-tax must be documented with foreign withholding certificates. DTA relief on outbound dividends is not a tax credit but a withholding tax reduction; attach the reduced-withholding application, TRC, and beneficial ownership declaration to support the lower rate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 / Box B-5 - Interim Prepayments and Balance Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset quarterly interim corporate tax payments, foreign branch tax payments, and any domestic withholding already paid
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean LLC paid provisional dividends to the foreign parent, WHT at the statutory rate must have been remitted as the LLC's withholding agent obligation. Reconcile withholding declarations to dividend resolutions and remit any balance through NTS payment identifiers; unpaid amounts accrue daily overdue surcharges

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 / Schedule of Cross-Border Related-Party Transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all controlled transactions with foreign related parties, including retainer fees, management charges, royalties, interest, cost recharges, and services paid to or received from non-residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report each international transaction in KRW, the relationship, transaction amount, pricing method, and supporting transfer-pricing documentation. Omission of a foreign parent or an SPV intermediary is a direct trigger for documentation penalties, TP adjustment, and criminal tax-evasion exposure

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers additional tax of 20% of the unfiled tax amount and a minimum penalty; negligent underreporting attracts 10% additional tax; intentional false underreporting attracts 20%. Overdue unpaid corporate tax accrues daily arrears (currently 0.022% per day). Criminal evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can lead to imprisonment for basic evasion and aggravated imprisonment up to 5 years for high-amount egregious schemes, plus fines and blacklisting of directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on non-resident dividends (20% national withholding plus 2% local surtax) absent treaty relief; applies to formal dividends, constructive dividends, and deemed capital distributions by the Korean LLC to foreign shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief the foreign shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its jurisdiction of residence for the relevant fiscal year; (2) execute a beneficial ownership declaration showing real economic owner and not a conduit or shell; (3) file the withholding tax reduction/exemption application with the NTS before payment or file a reclaim within 36 months; and (4) maintain substantive economic records in Korea - local premises, employees, management discretion, and core income-generating activities such as candidate sourcing, client negotiation, and placement contracts. NTS will deny treaty relief if the Korea-sourced income is routed to a no-tax or low-tax jurisdiction without economic substance
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT for interest and royalties paid to a non-resident without a Korean PE is 22% (20% national plus 2% local); typical Korean tax treaties reduce interest to 10-15% and royalties to 10-15%, subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits clauses; pure service fees for executive-search consulting are generally Korean-source business income taxable only if attributable to a Korean PE, but mischaracterized management fees are vulnerable to reclassification as royalties or disguised dividends and then WHT applies

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous Local File is generally required when annual revenue is at least KRW 50 billion and cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; Master File is generally required when annual revenue is at least KRW 100 billion and related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion; any executive-search LLC with foreign related-party transactions should maintain a contemporaneous functional analysis, benchmark study, and written transfer-pricing policy from the first transaction even below these thresholds to substantiate arm's-length pricing
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies substance-over-form and beneficial-ownership tests derived from the International Tax Coordination Act and OECD BEPS. Economic substance requires core income-generating activities to be performed in Korea through local staff, management, and offices; for an executive-search agency, CIGA include candidate sourcing, evaluation and vetting, client negotiation, fee setting, and contract execution. A Korean LLC acting only as a pass-through invoice shell for a foreign headhunting network will be disregarded, treaty benefits denied, and profits reallocated to the foreign principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and DTA Improper Dividend Strip
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC is used as a pure pass-through invoicing platform: the foreign parent holds no operating assets, no Korean employees exist, all executive-search services are performed offshore, and 85% of revenue is remitted as management fees or dividends to a low-tax jurisdiction while the Korean entity nevertheless claims treaty relief on an improperly obtained Tax Residency Certificate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS may disregard the entity under substance-over-form principles, recharacterize remittances as constructive dividends, impose 22% withholding plus penalties for failure to withhold, deny treaty benefits under anti-BEPS limitation-on-benefits and beneficial-ownership rules, levy 20% underreporting surcharges, and apply statutory daily arrears on the unpaid withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil when the LLC is a mere façade; the director is jointly and severally liable for unpaid withholding tax, civil restitution of the distributed funds, asset freezing and travel blacklisting, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 2 years for basic evasion and up to 5 years for aggravated evasion involving substantial amounts

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Management-Fee Overcharge
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC pays a 40% gross commission to the foreign parent as management consulting without an arm's-length benchmark, provides no contemporaneous Local File or Master File, supplies no service logs or staff records from the parent, and omits the controlled transaction from the NTS international-trade disclosure schedule while shifting taxable profit out of Korea
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 5 of the International Tax Coordination Act authorizes upward adjustment to arm's-length income; failure to maintain documentation can trigger penalty surcharges up to 30% of the supplemental tax amount, and failure to report overseas related-party transactions attracts separate additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director may be personally liable for damages under Commercial Act officer-liability rules, added as a joint collection obligor for the adjusted corporate tax, barred from leaving Korea during criminal tax investigation, and imprisoned for intentional tax evasion if the overcharge is found to be a fraudulent scheme

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Employment Placement and Cash-Transaction AML Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The entity charges KRW 5 billion in C-suite placement retainers without holding the mandatory paid-job-placement license under Korean employment placement law, directs foreign clients and candidates to wire retainers through Wise in increments below KRW 10 million to avoid AML reporting, and omits part of the cash or invoiced retainer revenue from the corporate income tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed paid job-placement brokerage is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to KRW 50 million under the Employment Security Act; tax fraud adds 20% unfiled return penalty, 10% underreporting penalty, daily arrears, and AML suspicious-transaction reporting fines under the Financial Transactions Report Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director faces personal criminal conviction for unauthorized employment placement, personal asset confiscation, blacklisting by the Ministry of Employment and Labor and the NTS, travel-ban enforcement, and veil-piercing civil liability where corporate funds are commingled with personal funds and retainer revenue is diverted
